$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Cosmos DB (SQL / Core API). See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.cosmos.account.crud.title: Database accounts (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.cosmos.data_explorer.title: Data Explorer: databases, containers and documents over the native Cosmos DB REST (SQL/Core API) data plane
limitations: The Cosmos data-plane store is a single keyspace shared by every Cosmos account in this Vyomi environment (no per-account partitioning) — a database id created under one account is visible from any other account's Data Explorer.

New Container accepts a hierarchical partition key request, a unique key policy and analytical store enablement the way the real form submits them, but only the indexing policy (on/off) round-trips for real; the others are accepted and not enforced.

azure.cosmos.query.title: SQL query (SELECT) over the Cosmos data plane
limitations: Covers a pragmatic SELECT subset: projection (incl. SELECT VALUE), TOP n, WHERE combining comparisons/IN/CONTAINS/STARTSWITH/ENDSWITH with a single logical operator throughout (AND-only or OR-only — mixed or parenthesized boolean expressions are not parsed), ORDER BY one field, OFFSET/LIMIT, and a top-level COUNT/VALUE COUNT aggregate; joins, subqueries, GROUP BY, other aggregate/system functions and stored procedures are not implemented.

azure.cosmos.default_consistency.title: Default consistency level
limitations: properties.consistencyPolicy is ENFORCED at the ARM contract level (defaultConsistencyLevel must be one of the 5 real values; BoundedStaleness requires maxStalenessPrefix in [10, 2147483647] and maxIntervalInSeconds in [5, 86400], same range Azure validates) — but every data-plane read in Vyomi is already strongly consistent, regardless of the configured level.

azure.cosmos.replicate_data_globally.title: Replicate data globally (region list, failover)
limitations: Add region and Manual Failover are ENFORCED for real: properties.locations is validated (unique region names, a 0-based gap-free failoverPriority sequence) and failoverPriorityChange really reassigns which region is failoverPriority 0. Vyomi still has one logical region underneath, so an added region never gets its own separately provisioned data-plane copy, and Service-Managed (automatic) Failover is an honest 'Not simulated' gap — Vyomi never triggers a failover on its own.

azure.cosmos.backup_restore.title: Backup & Restore policy
limitations: properties.backupPolicy is ENFORCED at the ARM contract level (backupPolicy.type, the Periodic interval/retention/redundancy ranges, the Continuous tier enum, and Azure's one-way Continuous-to-Periodic migration block all match the real API), but Vyomi never actually takes or restores a backup.

azure.cosmos.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the database account
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this account); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.cosmos.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered ARM mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill). The timespan picker is ENFORCED (narrowing it to e.g. 'Last hour' really drops older events via eventTimestamp ge on the query), but severity/category filtering is not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.cosmos.iam.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list is now ENFORCED scoped to this account (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view) instead of the whole subscription; Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation is still not modelled — Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment.
